claims.text: A single unified mechanism explains both the stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed unified mechanism involves thermal-expansion mismatch, solidification-induced thermal stresses, cold rolling, and aging.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is polycrystalline.
The initial material may have varying degrees of cold work and aging.
Thermal-expansion mismatch during composite solidification generates thermal stresses.
Solidification-related thermal-expansion mismatch and thermal stresses govern the stress–strain response of HfNbTaTiZr.
Solidification-related thermal-expansion mismatch and thermal stresses govern the thermoelastic response of HfNbTaTiZr.
Cold rolling influences the mechanical hardening or microhardness of HfNbTaTiZr.
Aging influences the hardening or microhardness of HfNbTaTiZr.
Cold rolling and aging interact with solidification-induced thermal stresses to change stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior.
The proposed experiment will measure thermal-expansion mismatch, thermal stresses, microhardness, and hardening after cold rolling and aging.
The baseline is HfNbTaTiZr behavior in the absence of thermal-expansion mismatch and solidification-induced thermal stresses.
The relevant response boundary is 293–1250 K.
A lack of correlation between measured thermal mismatch or thermal stress and post-processing hardness changes would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions permit testing up to 1250 °C, equivalent to approximately 1523 K, while the stated boundary ends at 1250 K. Thus the specified boundary excludes part of the stated test range.
